WorldFork social-state schema is being applied to a sports forecasting case, so sociology fields are lightweight and mainly audience-facing.

simulation_brief.decision_frame: terminal endpoint is whether Team T wins the series before Team L does
simulation_brief.summary: Team T, a Canadian club, begins a best-of-seven 2025 championship series against Team L, a defending champion with deep pitching and recent postseason experience. Team T has home-field energy and a strong offense. Series outcome depends on first team to four wins, with path dependence from pitching rotation, bullpen fatigue, and travel.
uncertainty_notes: No game-by-game roster, injury, or starting pitcher specifics provided at T0.
Outcome is explicitly unresolved at initialization and highly path-dependent across up to seven games.
Source corpus provides only coarse comparative strengths, so actor traits and graph weights are calibrated conservatively.

sociology_baseline.evidence: Supporters update around prior loyalties and known strengths rather than fully converging at T0.
Fan expression and engagement likely intensify after decisive game swings rather than staying flat.
Sports context has relatively low penalty for open opinion expression, though less-attached neutrals remain quieter.
Supporter communities cluster around team identity and reinforce favorable interpretations.
Momentum narratives usually require repeated game evidence and broad commentary amplification.
Team allegiance strongly structures interpretation of the same series events.
Attention should remain high during the series, with only modest decay between games unless contest becomes lopsided.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Public interpretation updates after each game because the series is a multi-step contest rather than a single result.
Rotation choices and bullpen fatigue can reshape perceived odds after each game.
Team T begins with a supportive atmosphere that may raise early enthusiasm and narrative tailwinds.
Team L enters with legitimacy and composure advantages in public framing.
Travel is a contextual stressor that can modestly shift fatigue and preparation narratives across games.
